# Tables

Each table of addresses, jumps and words, entry by entry. An RTS table holds each target minus 1; the target column gives the target. Index: [the reference](index.md).

<a id="sprite_buffer_addresses"></a>
## [`sprite_buffer_addresses`](../../src/actor/actor_sprites.asm#L309) `$274F-$2762`

*addresses*

Sprite image addresses, 10 words: entries 0-4 = sprites 0-4 in buffer 0 (sprite_buf_a_spr0..4), entries 5-9 = sprites 0-4 in buffer 1 (sprite_buf_b_spr0..4). Indexed by 2*(sprite + 5*buffer).

- **Read by:** [`set_sprite_buffer_pointer`](modules/actor/actor_sprites.md#set_sprite_buffer_pointer) [`$270E`](../../src/actor/actor_sprites.asm#L268), [`set_sprite_buffer_pointer`](modules/actor/actor_sprites.md#set_sprite_buffer_pointer) [`$2713`](../../src/actor/actor_sprites.asm#L270)

<a id="message_ptrs"></a>
## [`message_ptrs`](../../src/text/messages.asm#L11) `$43BE-$4487`

*addresses*

Message pointer table: 101 words, index = message number (A of print_message; the room code calls a message a tile). print_message points data_ptr at message - Y so that (data_ptr),Y with the start offset Y reads the first byte; X = text line (text_line_top_lo), Y = offset in the line (0-39 top row, 40-79 the row below). Message format: one byte per cell, ended by $A0. Cell code = (byte - $20) AND $7F; the code goes to the top row of the text line and code OR $80 (the bottom half of the double-height font) to the bottom row. So ASCII letters, digits and punctuation print as text, and the other bytes select graphic characters.

- **Read by:** [`print_message`](modules/actor/actor_driver_text.md#print_message) [`$17EB`](../../src/actor/actor_driver_text.asm#L66), [`print_message`](modules/actor/actor_driver_text.md#print_message) [`$17F3`](../../src/actor/actor_driver_text.asm#L70)

<a id="room_map_ptr_lo"></a>
## [`room_map_ptr_lo`](../../src/room/room_tables.asm#L69) `$4B34-$4B5D`

*addresses-split*

Room map addresses, low bytes then high bytes (21 entries: rooms 0-19 and the end of the last map $7FE0). draw_room reads the map of the current room. Map format: a byte with bit 7 clear is a run: count = byte, then one cell code drawn count times; a byte with bit 7 set is a literal block: count = byte AND $7F (0 = end of map) cell codes follow. Each cell is a double-height char: code on the top row, code OR $80 on the row below (codes with bit 7 set also go through map_tile_set_black). 40 cells per row pair (room_draw_step_cell).

- **Read by:** [`draw_room`](modules/room/draw_room.md#draw_room) [`$0AAF`](../../src/room/draw_room.asm#L158), [`draw_room`](modules/room/draw_room.md#draw_room) [`$0AB4`](../../src/room/draw_room.asm#L160)

<a id="lantern_list_ptr"></a>
## [`lantern_list_ptr`](../../src/room/lantern_lists.asm#L13) `$4CE2-$4D0B`

*addresses*

Per-room pointer to the room's lantern list (21 words: rooms 0-19 and a spare list). Lantern list format: 4-byte records ended by $FF: +0 state: 1 = lantern present, 0 = collected (reset_all_lanterns sets all to 1 at a game start) +1 replacement cell code drawn when the lantern is collected (top = AND $7F, bottom = OR $80) +2 column (Y offset in the text line), +3 text line. check_lantern_pickup finds a present lantern at a column/line, clears its state, decrements room_lanterns_left+room and returns the replacement code; setup_room_lanterns_and_init draws the collected lanterns of the room when the room is drawn.

- **Read by:** [`swap_room_lanterns`](modules/game/game_setup.md#swap_room_lanterns) [`$1007`](../../src/game/game_setup.asm#L114), [`swap_room_lanterns`](modules/game/game_setup.md#swap_room_lanterns) [`$100C`](../../src/game/game_setup.asm#L116), [`check_lantern_pickup`](modules/room/lantern_pickup.md#check_lantern_pickup) [`$3328`](../../src/room/lantern_pickup.asm#L23), [`check_lantern_pickup`](modules/room/lantern_pickup.md#check_lantern_pickup) [`$332D`](../../src/room/lantern_pickup.asm#L25), [`setup_room_lanterns_and_init`](modules/room/lantern_pickup.md#setup_room_lanterns_and_init) [`$3372`](../../src/room/lantern_pickup.asm#L83), [`setup_room_lanterns_and_init`](modules/room/lantern_pickup.md#setup_room_lanterns_and_init) [`$3377`](../../src/room/lantern_pickup.asm#L85), [`reset_room_lanterns`](modules/room/lantern_pickup.md#reset_room_lanterns) [`$33DA`](../../src/room/lantern_pickup.asm#L161), [`reset_room_lanterns`](modules/room/lantern_pickup.md#reset_room_lanterns) [`$33DF`](../../src/room/lantern_pickup.asm#L163)

<a id="frame_gfx_lo"></a>
## [`frame_gfx_lo`](../../src/actor/actor_frame_gfx_tables.asm#L10) `$59BD-$5B60`

*addresses-split*

Address of the 1-bit graphics of each of the 210 animation frames: 210 low bytes here, 210 high bytes at frame_gfx_hi. Frames 0-69 Bruce, 70-139 Yamo, 140-209 Ninja. Even frame = first sprite, odd frame = second sprite of the same pose (the Ninja uses only even frames; his odd entries are $0000). Readers: setup_sprite_frame (patches the LDA operands of the sprite builder copy_sprite_frame) and expand_contact_mask (start-up builder of the contact masks).

<a id="hw_nmi_vector"></a>
## [`hw_nmi_vector`](../../src/irq/hardware_vectors.asm#L7) `$FFFA-$FFFF`

*addresses*

CPU hardware vectors in the RAM under the KERNAL ROM (the ROM is switched out): NMI and RESET point to nmi_entry (an RTI), IRQ points to irq_entry (the raster interrupt handler).

- **Read by:** [`unused_jump_reset_vector`](modules/leftovers/leftover_1117.md#unused_jump_reset_vector) [`$1117`](../../src/leftovers/leftover_1117.asm#L9), `$EF29`

| Index | At | Value | Target |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | [`$FFFA`](../../src/irq/hardware_vectors.asm#L8) | `$1116` | [`nmi_entry` `$1116`](../../src/irq/interrupt_entry.asm#L25) |
| 1 | [`$FFFC`](../../src/irq/hardware_vectors.asm#L10) | `$1116` | [`nmi_entry` `$1116`](../../src/irq/interrupt_entry.asm#L25) |
| 2 | [`$FFFE`](../../src/irq/hardware_vectors.asm#L12) | `$1103` | [`irq_entry` `$1103`](../../src/irq/interrupt_entry.asm#L10) |
